solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Capital avenue (5)

blocks.note: capital as money, the wealth someone has to spend
an avenue as a way of getting to an end, a method

annotation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings. "Capital avenue" reads as a grand street in a capital city, but capital is money and an avenue is a route to an end.
annotation.definitionFit: Means can be wealth (a man of means) or a method (a means to an end).

entries.clue: Very small computers with integrated circuit must include PC (11)

indicatorNotes.must include: one thing including another holds it inside, so COP sits between MICROS and IC

blocks.note: micros are microcomputers
a PC is a police constable, a cop
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A tech note about tiny computers whose chips have to include a PC.
annotation.walkthrough: PC wants to be a personal computer, which fits the computing surface; here it is a police constable, and so a COP.
annotation.definitionFit: Microscopic means so small it can only be seen under a microscope, so very small.

entries.clue: Gemstone found in a street up north (5)

blocks.note: used as it stands
in northern English and Scots place names, gate means street, as in York's Stonegate

annotation.surface: A precious stone turns up on a street in the north of England.
annotation.walkthrough: "Up north" is not a direction here; it flags a northern dialect word. In York and other northern towns, gate is the old word for a street.
annotation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone.

entries.clue: Noteworthy painting, one you may find arresting (7,9)

blocks.note: noteworthy means out of the ordinary, special
a Constable is a painting by John Constable, the English landscape painter

annotation.surface: A remarkable painting, the sort that stops you in your tracks.
annotation.walkthrough: "Arresting" looks like praise for the picture, meaning striking; the definition takes it literally, as making arrests. A special constable is a volunteer part-time police officer in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A special constable is a volunteer police officer, someone who may arrest you.

entries.clue: Speaker from memory, perhaps one moving in speech (7)

indicatorNotes.in speech: said in speech, the word is heard rather than seen, so its sound counts

blocks.note: someone who re-sites a thing moves it to a new site, so a re-siter is perhaps one moving

annotation.surface: A speaker who talks from memory, maybe someone who is moving when they speak.
annotation.walkthrough: "Re-siter" is an invented word, one who re-sites or relocates, which is why the clue says "perhaps". It sounds exactly like reciter.
annotation.definitionFit: A reciter delivers poems or passages from memory.

entries.clue: Brighton school managed without dictionary — English (7)

indicatorNotes.without: without can mean outside, so RAN goes around the dictionary and English

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
the Oxford English Dictionary
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A Brighton school got by without a dictionary, just English.
annotation.walkthrough: "Without" reads as lacking, but here it is the older sense of outside. Roedean is a famous girls' boarding school on the coast near Brighton.
annotation.definitionFit: Roedean School stands on the cliffs just east of Brighton.

entries.clue: Admitted fish is eating starter of nothing ordinary (9)

indicatorNotes.is eating: whatever eats something has it inside, so COD holds N and FESSE
indicatorNotes.starter of: the starter is the first course, so the first letter of nothing

blocks.note: a common fish
first letter of nothing
in heraldry an ordinary is a simple band on a shield, and the fesse is the horizontal one

annotation.surface: Someone owns up that a fish is eating a plain starter of nothing much.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ordinary" wants to be O, or plain; it is a heraldry term for the basic bands on a coat of arms, and the fesse runs across the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both past-tense verbs mean owned up to a fault or crime.

entries.clue: In full colour, highly decorated capital in Attica missing edges (12)

indicatorNotes.in: RICH and ROMA go inside the trimmed Attica
indicatorNotes.missing edges: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, so ATTICA loses both A's

blocks.note: rich decoration is lavish and ornate
Rome, the Italian capital, in Italian
ATTICA without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A richly painted column capital in ancient Attica, its edges chipped away.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital here reads as the top of a Greek column, which suits Attica, but it is a capital city, Roma. Attica is the region round Athens.
annotation.definitionFit: Trichromatic means using three primary colours, which together give full colour.

entries.clue: Solid is decomposing with ray in this (10)

annotation.definition: Solid is decomposing with ray in this

indicatorNotes.decomposing: to decompose is to break down into parts, so SOLID IS falls apart

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, added by 'with'

annotation.surface: A description of a solid breaking down under a beam of radiation.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of SOLID IS and RAY break down together, just as the process breaks down matter.
annotation.definitionFit: Radiolysis is the breaking down of a substance by radiation.

entries.clue: Back under cover before food? Not sure (9)

indicatorNotes.Back: going back means running in the opposite direction, so ABED is written backwards

blocks.note: abed means in bed, under the covers
a table is the food served, as in keeping a good table

annotation.surface: Going back to bed before breakfast, and not sure it is a good idea.
annotation.walkthrough: TABLE for food is an old sense: a house that keeps a good table serves good meals.
annotation.definitionFit: Something debatable is open to question, so not sure.

entries.clue: Revealed the age of Father Edward (5)

blocks.note: da is an informal word for dad
Ted is a pet form of Edward

annotation.surface: Father Edward's appearance gave away how old he was.
annotation.walkthrough: "Father Edward" reads as a priest's title; the two words work separately, each as a family pet name.
annotation.definitionFit: To date something is to reveal its age, as a slang word dates a speaker.

entries.clue: Theft of college grant, grand left for student initially (8)

indicatorNotes.left for: one thing left in place of another replaces it, so G and L take the place of S
indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letter of student is used

blocks.note: a bursary is a grant to a student
a grand is a thousand pounds, G for short
standard abbreviation
first letter of student, which comes out

annotation.surface: A student's college grant was stolen, with a grand gone.
annotation.walkthrough: "Left" looks like the verb, what the thief left, but it is L, going in with G where the S of BURSARY was.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: burglary is the kind of stealing done by breaking into a building.

entries.clue: Big island fish new around Western Australia (6)

indicatorNotes.around: to go around something is to surround it, so TAI and N sit either side of WA

blocks.note: the tai is a Japanese sea bream
the state's abbreviation
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A big island and a fish newly caught off Western Australia.
annotation.walkthrough: TAI is the Japanese sea bream, a crossword regular that is rarely seen elsewhere.
annotation.definitionFit: Taiwan is a large island off the south-east coast of China.

entries.clue: Wild animals eating everyone on earth — pay careful attention (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.eating: whatever eats something has it inside, so BEARS holds ALL and E

blocks.note: bears are wild animals
all means everyone
E is the electrical symbol for earth

annotation.surface: A warning that wild animals are devouring everyone on the planet, so listen up.
annotation.walkthrough: "Earth" gives E, the abbreviation for an earth wire in British electrics.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who is all ears is listening eagerly, every part of them tuned in.

entries.clue: Solution for transferring power: make Roly an MP on 50 per cent of vote? (11)

indicatorNotes.50 per cent of: half of the four letters of vote, the back half

blocks.note: voters make someone an MP by electing them, so this is ELECT ROLY
the second half of VOTE

annotation.surface: A political plan for handing over power: get Roly elected with half the vote.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all politics, and "transferring power" sounds like a handover of government; it is electric power carried through a liquid. "Make Roly an MP" is ELECT ROLY.
annotation.definitionFit: A liquid that carries an electric current through its ions, as in a battery, is exactly this.

entries.clue: What can change appearance of each lemon when processed? (9)

indicatorNotes.when processed: processing turns something into something else, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A question about what makes a lemon look different once it has been processed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about fruit in a factory; the letters of EACH LEMON become the lizard famous for changing colour.
annotation.definitionFit: A chameleon is a lizard that changes the colour of its skin.

entries.clue: Tea and dinnertime are changing, not fixed (13)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, with 'and' joining

annotation.surface: A household notice that teatime and dinnertime are being moved about.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is its own joke: mealtimes that keep changing are exactly not fixed.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe something left undecided or unsettled.

entries.clue: Past issue linked to opera company going west (3-4)

indicatorNotes.going west: in an across answer west is leftwards, so EMIT and ENO are read backwards

blocks.note: to issue is to emit
English National Opera

annotation.surface: An old matter linked to an opera company heading west on tour.
annotation.walkthrough: "Going west" reverses both parts together: EMIT plus ENO, read backwards, gives ONETIME.
annotation.definitionFit: One-time means former, as in a one-time champion, so past.

entries.clue: Somehow hit dome bone of the skull (7)

indicatorNotes.Somehow: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are arranged in some other way

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Somebody hit their head, the dome of the skull.
annotation.walkthrough: The dome sounds like the skull itself, which suits the definition; the answer is a small bone deep inside it, between the eyes.
annotation.definitionFit: The ethmoid is the bone at the root of the nose that separates the nasal cavity from the brain.

entries.clue: Flier allowed to follow the French audio frequency (7)

blocks.note: le is French for the
standard abbreviation
let means allowed, and 'to follow' puts it after LE and AF

annotation.surface: A pilot is permitted to follow the French radio frequency.
annotation.walkthrough: "Flier" looks like a pilot or a bird; it is a printed handout, also spelt flyer.
annotation.definitionFit: A flier or flyer is a leaflet handed out to advertise something.

entries.clue: Be brief, how does one make saga sag? (3,1,4,5,5)

annotation.definition2: how does one make saga sag?

blocks.note: the everyday phrase for getting to the point

blocks.clueFragment: how does one make saga sag?
blocks.note: a saga is a long story; cut its last letter short and it becomes SAG

annotation.surface: Advice to keep it brief: how do you make a long saga drag less?
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is read literally: take the long story SAGA and cut it short by one letter, leaving SAG.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom said when skipping the details to get to the point; read literally, it describes trimming SAGA to SAG.

entries.clue: That place cast regularly enters? (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one
indicatorNotes.enters: to enter is to go into, so AT goes into THERE

blocks.note: there means that place
the second and fourth letters of cAsT

annotation.surface: A question about the place where the cast goes in night after night.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a theatre is that place the cast enters regularly. "Regularly" does double duty as the every-other-letter signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre is where a cast of actors turns up for every performance.

entries.clue: Short cavalryman with popular Arabic name (7)

indicatorNotes.Short: a word cut short loses its last letter, so HUSSAR loses its R

blocks.note: a hussar is a light cavalry soldier; cut short, he loses the R
what is in is fashionable, popular

annotation.surface: A short cavalry soldier who has a well-known Arabic name.
annotation.walkthrough: "Popular" seems to describe the name, but it is the wordplay: IN, as in the in thing.
annotation.definitionFit: Hussain, or Hussein, is a common Arabic given name.

entries.clue: Husband with a large ring, a light one (4)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
used as it stands
standard abbreviation, as on clothing sizes
O is ring-shaped

annotation.surface: A husband with a big wedding ring, but a light one.
annotation.walkthrough: "A light one" points back to "ring": a halo is a ring of light. "Light" reads as not heavy, which suits the jewellery.
annotation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light, as round a saint's head or the moon.

entries.clue: Oh, infant actor too involved in play from Tennessee (3,2,1,3,3,4)

annotation.answer: CAT ON A HOT TIN ROOF

indicatorNotes.involved: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Surprise that a child actor is also in a play from the American South.
annotation.walkthrough: "From Tennessee" suggests a play set in the state; it means from Tennessee Williams, the playwright.
annotation.definitionFit: Tennessee Williams wrote this 1955 drama of the Pollitt family, so it is a play from him.

entries.clue: Like original software? Deplore ad for a new version (3-6)

indicatorNotes.for a new version: a new version of something is a reworking of it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A complaint about an advert for the next version of some software.
annotation.walkthrough: "A new version" fits the software surface perfectly, and it is also the rearrangement signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Original software is the software that comes pre-loaded on a new computer.

entries.clue: Run down in power of past queen in time (6)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so ER goes inside DATE

blocks.note: a date is a point in time
Elizabeth Regina, Elizabeth II, now a past queen

annotation.surface: Reduced in power in the days of a former queen.
annotation.walkthrough: "Past" marks ER as a queen who has gone, Elizabeth II.
annotation.definitionFit: To derate machinery is to reduce its rated power.

entries.clue: Among pyramids, tomb hides (6)

indicatorNotes.hides: the phrase keeps the answer out of sight inside it

blocks.note: pyrAMIDS Tomb

annotation.surface: Somewhere among the pyramids, a tomb is hidden.
annotation.walkthrough: The Egyptian surface is pure dressing; the answer runs across the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both prepositions mean surrounded by, in the middle of.

entries.clue: Damage pitch with mud and water (6)

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
to shy a ball is to pitch or throw it

annotation.surface: A football pitch ruined by mud and water.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pitch" reads as a playing field, which the mud suits; it is the verb, to throw, SHY.
annotation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is soft and wet, full of mud and water.

entries.clue: What European is wearing casual shirt for a laugh? (3-3)

indicatorNotes.is wearing: whatever wears a shirt is inside it, so EH and E go into TEE

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
eh? is a way of saying what?
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A question: what is a European wearing a T-shirt for, as a joke?
annotation.walkthrough: "What" looks like the start of a question, but it is EH, as in "Eh? What did you say?"
annotation.definitionFit: The word imitates the sound of a stifled giggle.

entries.clue: Disastrous answer thanks, tantrum’s in with it? (12)

indicatorNotes.in: A, TA and STROP go inside CHIC

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
ta is informal British for thanks
a strop is a fit of bad temper
with it means fashionable, chic

annotation.surface: A disastrous reply of thanks, with a tantrum thrown in.
annotation.walkthrough: "With it" looks like a link but is a single meaning: fashionable, CHIC, which wraps round the rest. "Tantrum's in" is tantrum is in.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both adjectives describe something ruinous on a large scale.

entries.clue: Saw pair finished book (7)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
something over is finished
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A couple of people saw a book through to the end.
annotation.walkthrough: "Saw" reads as the past of see; it is the noun, an old saying.
annotation.definitionFit: An old sense of the noun saw is a traditional saying, a piece of folk wisdom.

entries.clue: What could be Brighton line is pursuing speed (10)

blocks.note: to race is to speed
a course is a line taken; pursuing puts it after RACE

annotation.surface: The Brighton railway line is chasing a faster service.
annotation.walkthrough: "Brighton line" suggests the railway to the south coast, but the definition stops at Brighton, which has a horse racecourse on the hills above the town.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: racegoers call a track by its town's name, so Brighton is one.

entries.clue: Drink container upended, about to be dispensed with (7)

indicatorNotes.upended: in a down answer, turning something on its end reads it from the bottom up
indicatorNotes.to be dispensed with: what is dispensed with is done without, so the C for about is dropped

blocks.note: a canister is a container
c, circa, means about; it is dropped from the end

annotation.surface: A drinks container turned upside down, about to be thrown away.
annotation.walkthrough: "About" looks like part of "about to", something that is going to happen; it is C, short for circa.
annotation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

entries.clue: Work to which Edentata might provide answer, if split? (8,4)

blocks.note: the zoological name for sloths, anteaters and armadillos, which has nothing to do with the answer
break the word into two: the garden of Genesis followed by a British farewell

annotation.surface: An odd suggestion that a group of toothless mammals holds the key to a famous work.
annotation.walkthrough: Edentata is the old name for the order of sloths and armadillos, but split in two it reads EDEN TA-TA: goodbye to Eden, so paradise lost. Ta-ta is British slang for goodbye.
annotation.definitionFit: Paradise Lost is John Milton's epic poem about the fall of man from Eden.

entries.clue: Safeguard share of Native Americans according to Spooner (10)

indicatorNotes.according to Spooner: Dr Spooner famously swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: the Cree are a Native American people and a portion is a share; swap the opening sounds

annotation.surface: Protecting the share that belongs to Native Americans.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the C and P sounds of CREE PORTION and you say PREE CORSHUN. The Cree are an indigenous people of Canada and the northern US.
annotation.definitionFit: A precaution is a measure taken in advance to safeguard against harm.

entries.clue: Overblown nature of dahlia mostly the centre of lush head (11)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so POMPON loses its last letter

blocks.note: a pompon is a kind of dahlia with small round flowers; most of it
the two middle letters of lUSh
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

annotation.surface: A dahlia's showy blooms and a lush flower head, all a bit much.
annotation.walkthrough: "Head" looks like a flower head in this garden surface; it is a headland, NESS, as in place names like Dungeness.
annotation.definitionFit: Pompousness is an inflated, self-important manner, an overblown nature.

entries.clue: Once compelled the art editor to be fearful (5-7)

blocks.note: fain is an old word, once meaning obliged or compelled
used as it stands
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: At one time the art editor was forced to be scared.
annotation.walkthrough: "Once" marks an archaic word: FAIN, which could mean obliged as well as glad.
annotation.definitionFit: Faint-hearted means timid, lacking courage, so fearful.

entries.clue: Pickwickian place of idyll and legend, possibly (7,4)

indicatorNotes.possibly: the letters could possibly be arranged another way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, with 'and' joining

annotation.surface: A place in Pickwick that is part rural idyll and part legend.
annotation.walkthrough: Dingley Dell is the country home of Mr Wardle in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers, an idyll in the novel, which makes the surface fit.
annotation.definitionFit: Dingley Dell is Mr Wardle's farm in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.

entries.clue: Stretch out uniform ahead of camp accommodating an officer (10)

indicatorNotes.ahead of: one thing ahead of another comes before it, so LIE and U precede the camp
indicatorNotes.accommodating: to accommodate is to give room to, so TENT holds AN

blocks.note: to lie down is to stretch out
U is uniform in the radio alphabet
a tent is somewhere to camp
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A soldier stretches out his uniform in camp, where an officer is housed.
annotation.walkthrough: "An" belongs to the wordplay, going into TENT, so the definition is just officer. "Uniform" wants to be army dress; it is U in the phonetic alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the rank sits just above second lieutenant, among the junior commissioned ranks.

entries.clue: Going over support in wood and stone (6)

indicatorNotes.Going over: going back over the letters reads them in reverse
indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so BRA goes inside ELM

blocks.note: elm is a wood
a bra is a support garment

annotation.surface: Going over a support beam set in wood and stone.
annotation.walkthrough: BRA goes into ELM to make ELBRAM, and the whole thing is then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Marble is a hard stone used for sculpture and building.

entries.clue: Concerned with not entirely reliable chap appearing again (9)

indicatorNotes.not entirely: not the entire word, so SURE loses its last letter

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in a memo heading
sure means reliable; not entirely, it loses the E
a gent is a chap

annotation.surface: Worried about a rather unreliable man who keeps turning up.
annotation.walkthrough: "Not entirely reliable" reads as a judgement on the chap; it is an instruction to cut the last letter from SURE.
annotation.definitionFit: From Latin resurgere, to rise again: something on the rise once more after a decline.

entries.clue: What one uses to see down answer hasn’t succeeded (6)

indicatorNotes.hasn’t: the answer lacks S, so the S is taken out

blocks.note: the answer to a down clue, 31 down
S is short for succeeded, as in family trees

annotation.surface: Something you see with, and a gloomy note that an answer has failed.
annotation.walkthrough: "Down answer" points to another answer in the grid without saying which: 31 down, RETSINA. "Down" looks like sad, which suits the failure.
annotation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.

entries.clue: One of two men introduced by a Pope (9)

blocks.note: a man's name, the first of the two
choosing one of two is either this or that
a man's name, the second of the two

annotation.surface: A man introduced to the Pope, one of a pair.
annotation.walkthrough: "One of two men" is read as GREG OR IAN: one or other of two men. The Gregorian calendar was introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582.
annotation.definitionFit: The Gregorian calendar and Gregorian chant take their names from popes called Gregory.

entries.clue: Relating to inheritance, client age needs to be sorted out (9)

indicatorNotes.needs to be sorted out: sorting out puts things in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A solicitor's note that a client's age has to be settled before an inheritance.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is legal: inheritance as a will. The answer is the biological sense, inheriting genes.
annotation.definitionFit: Genetical is an older form of genetic, relating to heredity.

entries.clue: Player, the rest of the eleven and I engaged in lechery (8)

indicatorNotes.engaged in: one thing engaged in another is inside it, so TEN and I go into LUST

blocks.note: lechery is lust
a team of eleven minus one leaves ten
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A cricketer, the rest of the team and I caught up in scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: "Player" and "eleven" suggest a cricket or football side; the player is a musician. The rest of the eleven, once one player is picked out, is TEN.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a musician whose instrument is the lute is one kind of player.

entries.clue: What takes hops in local site? (4)

indicatorNotes.takes hops: hopping over every other letter picks out the even ones

blocks.note: the even letters of lOcAl SiTe

annotation.surface: A question about which local spot the hops are taken to.
annotation.walkthrough: "Takes hops" does two jobs: an oast takes in hops to dry, and hopping along LOCAL SITE picks out every other letter. An oast house is a Kent kiln for drying hops.
annotation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln where hops are dried for brewing.

entries.clue: Many are supporting this vocally — are you? (5,5,8)

indicatorNotes.vocally: spoken aloud, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: the letters R U, the usual abbreviation for rugby union

annotation.surface: A crowd is cheering a team: are you one of them?
annotation.walkthrough: "Are you?" said out loud is R U, the standard abbreviation of the full answer. "Supporting" is being a fan, as in supporting a team.
annotation.definitionFit: Rugby union football is the fifteen-a-side game, with a huge following.

entries.clue: Well behaved attendant the German found in a Paris airport (7)

indicatorNotes.found in: something found in a place is inside it, so DER sits within ORLY

blocks.note: Orly is one of the two main Paris airports
der is German for the

annotation.surface: A polite airport attendant from Germany works at a Paris airport.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue has two definitions before its wordplay, so do not look for a single definition: "Well behaved attendant" is two separate meanings side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means disciplined and tidy; as a noun it is a hospital porter or a soldier who attends an officer.

entries.clue: Light-hearted talk limited in Taliban territory? (6)

indicatorNotes.limited in: the answer is confined within the phrase

blocks.note: taliBAN TERritory

annotation.surface: Wondering whether light-hearted chat is restricted under Taliban rule.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark is apt: banter is exactly what a Taliban regime might limit.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: good-humoured teasing and chat.

entries.clue: Most of arrested thrown in nick repeatedly (7)

indicatorNotes.Most of: most of the word, so ARRESTED loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.thrown: thrown about, the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: ARRESTED without its last letter, then rearranged

annotation.surface: Most of those arrested were thrown into a police cell again and again.
annotation.walkthrough: "Nick" is British slang for prison or a police station, which suits the arrests; here it is the verb, to cut notches.
annotation.definitionFit: To serrate is to give an edge a row of notches, to nick it repeatedly.

entries.clue: Bond got round M’s predecessor showing mercy (7)

indicatorNotes.got round: to get round something is to encircle it, so CEMENT surrounds L

blocks.note: cement bonds things together
L comes just before M in the alphabet

annotation.surface: James Bond got round his boss's predecessor, who showed mercy.
annotation.walkthrough: Bond and M are James Bond and his spy chief, but Bond is CEMENT and M is just a letter, whose predecessor is L.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a clement judge is lenient; the same root gives clemency.

entries.clue: Love drink I had (5)

blocks.note: a cup is a drink, as in fruit cup
I'd is short for I had

annotation.surface: A fond memory: love, the drink I had.
annotation.walkthrough: "Love" looks like an endearment; it is Cupid, the god of love.
annotation.definitionFit: The Roman god is love personified, and his name stands for it, as in Cupid's arrow.

entries.clue: Vacated draughty and dirty house (7)

indicatorNotes.Vacated: a vacated word is emptied of its middle, leaving the first and last letters

blocks.note: DraughtY with its inside emptied
nasty means dirty, foul

annotation.surface: An empty house left cold and filthy.
annotation.walkthrough: "House" reads as a building, which suits the draughts and dirt; it is a royal line, as in the House of Windsor.
annotation.definitionFit: A ruling family line is called a house, as in the House of Tudor.

entries.clue: Scarcely sufficient — that has a lot missing inside? (5)

indicatorNotes.has a lot missing inside: most of the middle of the phrase goes, leaving only the ends

blocks.note: SCArcely without its last five letters, the beginning of the phrase
the last two letters of sufficieNT, the end of the phrase

annotation.surface: Barely enough: is that because so much is missing from inside?
annotation.walkthrough: "That" points back to the words before it: the definition itself is the fodder, stripped down to its first three and last two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Scant means barely enough.

entries.clue: Keyboard instrument only audible when it has the lead? (8,5)

blocks.note: the surface suggests playing the lead part in a band

blocks.clueFragment: only audible when it has the lead?
